profiles: The pinned native releases. MySQL also uses completion_type=0 for omitted completion options. The fixture uses ordinary transactional tables and an autocommit connection before BEGIN.
scope: Plain begin, commit, rollback, savepoint, release and rollback-to statements. Named operations store the exact decoded label in their connection-local role.
open: Transaction characteristics and isolation clauses, chaining or connection release, prepared and XA transactions, session configuration, and lock and cursor observations

TransactionCommand.role: One of the six ordered connection-local transition roles
invariants: Every case has a fixed native SQL form
Savepoint, release and rollback-to have one checked name
MySQL labels use one to 64 non-NUL BMP characters. PostgreSQL labels use the checked nonempty UTF-8 identifier role and its 63-byte bound.
Transaction.meaning: Begin opens a transaction. When one is open, MySQL commits it before starting another. PostgreSQL keeps the current transaction and issues a warning. Commit publishes, and rollback discards its writes. A savepoint records the current transactional state. Rollback-to removes later work and retains its target. PostgreSQL releases the named savepoint with its successors. MySQL releases the named entry. PostgreSQL keeps older equal-name entries underneath the newest one. MySQL replaces an equal-name entry.
Transaction.sql: Emit the registered command and quote the decoded label when required. MySQL explicitly emits AND NO CHAIN NO RELEASE on commit and rollback.

analysis: Normalize equivalent plain command spellings. Accept omitted and explicitly non-chaining completion under the fixed profile. Reject transaction characteristics, positive chaining, connection release and other transaction forms. The active connection supplies the open transaction and savepoint stack when executed.
observations: Typed rows visible on the executing connection
Committed rows visible on an independent connection
Rollbacks to distinct checkpoints and equal-label reuse

finite.completeness: Check every combination of label, final terminal command and program role in the observed constructed operations.

faults: Make rollback-to use the other live checkpoint
trust: Fixed native profile and transactional fixture
Independent interpreter of local writes, visibility and checkpoint transitions
